forces.title: New EU Packaging & Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR)
forces.description: The new EU Regulation 2025/40 on Packaging and Packaging Waste (PPWR), effective from August 2026, introduces mandatory phased recyclability, labelling, and reporting requirements, and bans certain substances. This structural change compels all packaging producers and e-commerce retailers across the EU to adapt their materials and processes to ensure compliance, significantly impacting product design, manufacturing, and supply chains.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Elevated and volatile input costs for packaging materials
forces.description: The packaging industry faces severe headwinds from elevated and volatile input costs, including pulp, recovered fiber, wood, energy, petrochemicals, polymers, and aluminum. Price spikes and supply disruptions from geopolitical conflicts (e.g., Middle East), loss of Russian wood imports, and tighter fiber availability amplify production costs across paper, plastic, and metal packaging segments, severely impacting margins and competitiveness for European manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Reinventing the European pulp and paper operating model

forces.title: Sustainability demands driven by regulation, not consumer pull
forces.description: While consumers care about sustainability in packaging (recyclability, circularity), their willingness to pay a premium has weakened due to inflationary pressures. Consequently, sustainability investment for packaging companies is increasingly driven by regulatory mandates (e.g., PPWR) rather than broad consumer demand. This shifts sustainability from a market differentiator to a baseline compliance requirement, influencing product development and operational costs.
forces.source_title: Reinventing the European pulp and paper operating model

forces.title: Slowing demand, overcapacity, and increased global competition
forces.description: The European pulp and paper packaging industry faces a challenging environment characterized by slowing demand, persistent overcapacity across grades, and intensifying global competition. Excess supply from regions like Asia flowing into international markets limits opportunities for sustained price recovery and compresses margins for European producers. This necessitates a strong focus on operational efficiency and market differentiation to remain competitive.
forces.source_title: Reinventing the European pulp and paper operating model

forces.title: Integrated operating models & advanced analytics for efficiency
forces.description: European packaging companies can achieve competitive advantage through integrated operating models that connect demand sensing, supply chain planning, production scheduling, procurement, and commercial decisions. Leveraging AI and advanced analytics for optimizing mill operations, precise pricing, customer targeting, and site sprints can lead to substantial EBITDA improvements (3-15 percentage points), driving productivity, commercial discipline, and resilience in a volatile market.
forces.source_title: Reinventing the European pulp and paper operating model

forces.title: High reliance on imported raw materials in Irish paper & packaging
forces.description: Ireland's paper and packaging sector has limited upstream capacity and is heavily dependent on imported raw materials. This structural reliance exposes the sector to significant volatility in international raw material prices and increased logistics costs, limiting pricing power and eroding margins, particularly for smaller operators. Firms must manage stock levels and supplier resilience carefully to mitigate risks.

forces.title: US tariff-related competitiveness risks for Irish paper & packaging
forces.description: Irish paper and packaging firms serving export markets face specific risks from US tariff developments and international trade uncertainty. These factors can impact their competitiveness, reduce pricing power, and challenge their ability to recover input cost increases without weakening customer relationships. Firms must monitor trade policies and diversify where possible to mitigate these risks.

forces.title: Geopolitical realignment driving reshoring and local supply chains
forces.description: Geopolitically driven supply chain reorganization, including industrial reshoring in Europe, is causing a step change in domestic materials demand. This structural shift towards localized supply chains for materials like steel and aluminum creates opportunities for rigid metal packaging producers by ensuring more stable and accessible raw material supply, though it also requires adaptation to regional price volatility.
forces.source_title: The next wave of value in the materials supply chain

forces.title: Decarbonization redefining material specifications for packaging
forces.description: Decarbonization efforts are structurally redefining material specifications across industries, with global buyers aiming to increase 'green metals' share to 32% by 2030. This impacts rigid metal packaging producers, requiring them to adapt sourcing and production to offer differentiated products with carbon reporting, segregated green flows, and recycling integration to meet evolving corporate and regulatory sustainability commitments.
forces.source_title: The next wave of value in the materials supply chain

forces.title: CPG companies reducing inventory and increasing order volatility
forces.description: Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) companies, major customers for packaging, are reducing inventory levels and increasing order volatility while pushing for more-frequent pricing adjustments. This cyclical shift increases variability in packaging mill operations and places additional pressure on utilization, planning, and cost efficiency across the supply chain. Packaging producers must adapt to these demand patterns and manage risks.
forces.source_title: Resetting cost competitiveness in pulp and paper packaging

forces.title: Stricter EU regulations on food contact packaging materials
forces.description: EU Regulation 2025/351, coming into force later in 2026, will impose restrictions on chemicals and heavy metals used in food contact packaging. This structural change mandates packaging producers to adapt material compositions and manufacturing processes to ensure compliance, potentially leading to R&D and material sourcing adjustments for safety and regulatory adherence, impacting profitability and innovation.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Middle East conflict driving higher energy and raw material costs
forces.description: The Middle East conflict is causing significant inflation across global supply chains, leading to higher oil prices and freight costs. This directly elevates input costs for packaging production (e.g., petrochemicals, polymers for plastics; aluminum for cans) and indirectly impacts demand from food and beverage customers who face increased agricultural production costs. This creates widespread margin pressure for packaging manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Evolving tariffs slowing global packaging growth
forces.description: Forecasts from 2025 estimate that evolving tariffs could slow global packaging growth by up to 0.5% per annum, particularly impacting packaging segments heavily reliant on imports. This external shock adds to cost pressures and challenges the industry's profitability, necessitating strategic adjustments in sourcing and supply chain management for European packaging companies to mitigate adverse effects.
forces.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

forces.title: Rise of private-label and smaller CPG brands impacting packaging economics
forces.description: The sustained growth of private-label and smaller CPG companies, perceived as high quality by over 80% of US and European consumers, structurally reshapes packaging demand economics. While supporting unit demand, this shift often entails lower average selling prices, higher SKU complexity, larger pack sizes with less packaging, and a fragmented customer base, challenging packaging suppliers' margins and operational efficiency.
forces.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

viewpoints.title: Paper & Cardboard Packaging demand growth slowing, value replacing volume
viewpoints.description: McKinsey observes that packaging and specialty paper grades, while still resilient, are experiencing more selective growth. The anticipated shift from plastics to fiber-based solutions is slower than expected, indicating a structural preference for value over volume in this segment of the packaging market, leading to a cautious outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: Reinventing the European pulp and paper operating model

viewpoints.title: Italian packaging board benefits from e-commerce, exports, and sustainability trends
viewpoints.description: Packaging board constitutes over half of Italy's paper production, benefiting from tailwinds like e-commerce expansion, strong industrial exports, and ongoing sustainability-driven substitution trends. These factors position the segment as the largest and most strategic within Italy's pulp and paper market, indicating a positive outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: Reinventing the European pulp and paper operating model

viewpoints.title: Irish paper and packaging sector small, specialised, and facing cost pressures
viewpoints.description: Ireland's paper and packaging sector is small, highly specialised, and heavily reliant on imported raw materials, with activity concentrated in corrugated board, paper-based packaging, and niche processing. While sustainable packaging demand offers opportunities, the sector faces significant exposure to rising input and energy costs, alongside international trade and export market pressures, leading to a cautious negative outlook.

viewpoints.title: Pulp and paper packaging faces structural reset due to slowing demand and volatile costs
viewpoints.description: McKinsey states that the pulp and paper packaging industry is undergoing a structural reset, characterized by slowing demand, limited growth (due to geopolitical conflicts and tariffs), persistent overcapacity across various grades, and elevated volatility in input costs for fiber and energy. These factors are compressing margins and necessitating a new operational response beyond traditional cost tactics, leading to a negative outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: Resetting cost competitiveness in pulp and paper packaging

viewpoints.title: Operational rigor critical for pulp and paper packaging value creation amidst pricing limits
viewpoints.description: In the pulp and paper packaging sector, revenue growth has been price-driven, but persistent oversupply limits short-term headroom for further price increases. Value creation now increasingly depends on operational rigor, cost discipline, and the ability to adapt operating models to a volatile environment, underscoring a shift from volume-led to efficiency-led strategies, implying a cautious outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: Resetting cost competitiveness in pulp and paper packaging

viewpoints.title: Global packaging and paper industry reset, growth rebound not materialized
viewpoints.description: McKinsey identifies an industry-wide reset in the global packaging and paper sector since 2022, following a decade of steady growth. The anticipated rebound has not occurred; instead, it's characterized by flat/declining volumes, external shocks (tariffs, volatile raw material prices), and cautious consumer spending, all contributing to increased pressure and underlying operational inefficiencies, indicating a negative outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

viewpoints.title: Consumer willingness to pay for sustainable packaging remains constrained
viewpoints.description: McKinsey's global consumer survey (2025) shows that while consumers still care about sustainability (e.g., recyclability, recycled content), it has declined in importance relative to other purchasing factors, especially value for money. Willingness to pay a premium for sustainable packaging remains constrained across most segments, making regulatory drivers more influential than consumer pull, leading to a cautious negative outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

viewpoints.title: Decelerating growth and flat/negative margins across packaging substrates
viewpoints.description: The packaging industry is experiencing overall decelerating growth and nearly flat or slightly negative EBITDA margins across all major substrates (paper, plastics, glass, and metal). This is attributed to weak demand, persistent inflationary cost pressures, and underlying inefficiencies, signifying a challenging financial environment for packaging manufacturers and indicating a negative outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

viewpoints.title: Paper containerboard demand declining, but top players preserving margins
viewpoints.description: Demand volumes for paper containerboard have been declining since 2022, influenced by a shift in e-commerce towards flexible packaging, weak macroeconomic conditions, and trends in right-sized packaging and lightweighting. Despite this, top players in the segment have managed to preserve margins through high vertical integration and capacity rationalization, indicating a cautious positive outlook for resilient companies.
viewpoints.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

viewpoints.title: Rigid plastics packaging profitability deteriorating due to overcapacity and soft demand
viewpoints.description: The rigid plastics packaging industry is experiencing deteriorating profitability, especially in blow molding, due to soft Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) demand combined with persistent overcapacity. This imbalance has resulted in sustained pricing pressure, forcing companies to address commercial excellence and cost focus to counter the negative market dynamics, leading to a negative outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

viewpoints.title: Flexible plastics packaging shows innovation but faces oversupply and pricing pressure
viewpoints.description: Flexible plastics packaging continues to innovate with mono-materials and recycle-ready structures, sustaining customer engagement and sustainability positioning. However, similar to rigid plastics, the segment is challenged by oversupply, which exerts pressure on pricing. This necessitates a strong focus on commercial excellence, cost management, and differentiated capabilities to maintain profitability, resulting in a cautious negative outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry

demand_drivers.description: Growth in online retail continues to drive demand for packaging board.
Strong performance in industrial exports creates demand for packaging board.
Shift from non-paper materials to paperboard due to environmental concerns.

market_sizing.methodology: Packaging board represents just over half of Italian paper production, benefiting from e-commerce, industrial exports, and sustainability-driven substitution trends.

demand_drivers.description: Demand for paper and packaging is largely supported by Ireland's robust agrifood sector.
Consumer and regulatory preferences for sustainable options drive opportunities in the sector.

pnl_drivers.description: The sector is exposed to increasing costs for raw materials and energy, impacting profitability.

pnl_drivers.driver: International trade and export market pressures
pnl_drivers.description: Uncertainty and tariffs in international trade affect competitiveness and margins for exporters.

new_opportunities.description: Growing demand for environmentally friendly packaging presents new business opportunities.

demand_drivers.description: Supply chain reorganization and reshoring of industrial processes cause a step change in domestic materials demand.
Redefining material specifications, with increased demand for 'green metals'.

demand_drivers.driver: New technology (data centers, EVs, renewable energy)
demand_drivers.description: These sectors generate sustained high demand for steel, aluminum, and copper, requiring higher-quality materials.
Manufacturers increasingly outsource processing and logistics services, pushing demand to material wholesalers and service centers.
